negative_findings.description: WebFetch of https://bqk-kos.org/sistemet-e-pagesave/?lang=en returned HTTP 403 Forbidden. Other bqk-kos.org URLs are indexed by search engines and PDFs under /wp-content/uploads/ and /repository/docs/ resolve in search results.
negative_findings.result_summary: HYPOTHESIS: the CBK site is behind a WAF/bot filter that rejects non-browser user agents on HTML pages. Not evidence the site is dead. Collection will need a headless browser or realistic headers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most important source for this cell is the CBK site; an automated collector using naive HTTP will silently return zero content and be misread as 'no new regulation'.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Albanian for a CBK public-consultation channel for draft regulations ('projektrregullore', 'konsultim publik') and found no dedicated CBK consultation page in results; only the government-wide pre-legislative concept-document route and OPM/Assembly channels surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: No confirmed CBK-specific draft-regulation consultation portal. Draft regulations may be circulated to the industry (e.g. via the Banking Association) rather than published.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Consultations are an explicit topic in scope; if CBK does not publish drafts, the earliest observable signal is the Board approval press release, which shortens lead time on regulatory change to near zero.

negative_findings.description: Albanian and English searches for a Kosovo instant-payments regulation ('rregullore për pagesat e menjëhershme', 'instant payments regulation CBK') returned only a May 2026 CBK/KBA workshop and strategy-level statements, not a binding regulation or a mandated go-live date.
negative_findings.result_summary: As of this run, instant payments in Kosovo appear to be at infrastructure/strategy stage; no dated regulatory mandate located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Instant-payment mandates are the cell's highest-value deadline signal; its absence should be recorded as 'not yet issued', not assumed missing from the search.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language search ('Centralna banka Kosova propisi platni promet elektronski novac licenciranje') was dominated by Serbia/Montenegro central-bank content and dinar-related political coverage rather than CBK payments rulemaking.
negative_findings.result_summary: Serbian terminology is noisy for this cell: 'platni promet', 'uredba', 'CBK' collide with NBS/CBCG sources and with the dinar dispute. Only one CBK Serbian regulation PDF surfaced directly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Serbian coverage must be obtained by enumerating the CBK site's own 'SRB-' prefixed files and ?lang=sr variants rather than by open-web Serbian search.

negative_findings.description: No standalone public KIPS rulebook / participation agreement document was located; only the CBK web description of the four-phase accession process and the separate regulation on non-bank PSP access.
negative_findings.result_summary: The operational KIPS rulebook may be issued to participants rather than published on the open web.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Interbank clearing rules and cut-off/session changes would then be invisible to open-source collection and must be inferred from CBK web pages, annual reports, or industry sources.

brief: Kosovo's payments-regulation landscape is highly centralised on the Central Bank (BQK/CBK), whose Payment Systems Department publishes a distinct B-series of regulations, technical standards (IBAN, KOS-GIRO, QR code) and the National Retail Payments Strategy separately from prudential supervision material — but the site is WAF-protected and offers no visible draft-regulation consultation channel, so board-approval press releases and dated PDF uploads are the earliest observable signals. The second pillar is the legislative track: the PSD2-style Draft Law on Payment Services (Government Decision 08/08, 3 April 2026) moving through the Assembly and into the Official Gazette, with reporting that three related laws are pending before the Constitutional Court and blocking Kosovo's final SEPA application. The third pillar is external gatekeepers — the European Payments Council (versioned EPC409-09 country list and geographical-scope criteria) and DG FISMA — where Kosovo's SEPA admission will first become verifiable. Albanian is the working language of the primary corpus; Serbian versions exist on the CBK site under an 'SRB-' file prefix but open-web Serbian search is too noisy to rely on.
